source.title: Maximum Number of Groups Entering a Competition

teaching.hint: What is the fewest students that could support a chosen number of strictly growing group sizes?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The size rule gives a triangular-number lower bound, and positivity lets a sorted assignment satisfy the sum rule whenever the size bound is met.
solution_outline.approach: Find the largest `g` with `1+2+...+g <= n`. To establish achievability, sort grades conceptually and assign successive blocks of sizes `1,2,...,g-1`, then put the rest into the final group.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Every later block has more members, each no smaller than members in earlier blocks; its positive extra member makes its sum strictly greater.
solution_outline.correctness: Any `g` groups need at least the first `g` positive sizes, giving the upper bound. The sorted construction uses all students and satisfies both strict inequalities, so the bound is attained.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(sqrt n)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary space to compute the count; sorting is only a proof construction, not required by the algorithm.
solution_outline.pitfall: Ignoring the grade-sum condition without proving it follows from a suitable assignment is incomplete.

common_wrong_turns: Assuming arbitrary grouping satisfies increasing sums
Sorting grades in the implementation unnecessarily
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained positivity, all-students requirement, strict inequalities, and free assignment order.
